newsitem.title: USA: TWA confirms job cuts at Kennedy Airport.
newsitem.headline: TWA confirms job cuts at Kennedy Airport.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc on Monday confirmed a published report that the nation's seventh largest airline will eliminate some jobs at its hub at Kennedy International Airport in New York.

TWA spokesman John McDonald confirmed a report in Monday's Wall Street Journal that efforts to reduce losses on TWA's trans-Atlantic flights will include job cuts, although the exact number has yet to be determined.
TWA is also expected to take a charge against earnings in future quarters, McDonald confirmed.
"We're talking to several parties on how to best use our domestic hangar at Kennedy," McDonald said, "But I have not seen anything to confirm the 10-percent figure (cited) in the story."

The article, based on an interview with Roden Brandt, TWA senior vice president of planning and marketing, said the plan would shrink TWA's capacity by 10 percent and reduce overall costs by about $400 million a year. TWA had already announced plans to reduce the number of feeder flights to New York from seven U.S. cities and reduce connections from California.
The article said fewer than 1,000 employees would be affected. Workers with more tenure will be able to transfer to other positions, although junior workers may be displaced, the report said.
McDonald told Reuters no jobs would be affected before mid-January.
"We should have more information and a figure on how many jobs will be affected by mid-January," McDonald said.
